notes: The ground clutter of the camera's ring (simcore/scenery/clutter.hpp, roadmap T6.1 and L5): the ring and the kinds of plant and clod. Where they go, and how many, is the land's recipes' (data/scenery/recipes/, simcore/scenery/recipes.hpp, roadmap L2): each ground layer's recipe scatters these kinds over its bands. Game values judged by eye (Pannonia is fictional: the look, not the statistics); presentation only, nothing in the simulation reads it. Thin plants are drawn as crossed alpha cards (art/clutter, tools/make_cards.py), so a plant here is a clump: its width is a clump's and its density a clump's. Each 4 m cell draws its candidates from its own position (the same for every client, and the same when the ring moves back over it), each kept while its fixed threshold is under 1 / (1 + (d / falloff_m)^2) at its distance d from the camera. A kind's part is a mesh in scenery/map_meshes.hpp (ClutterMesh) that a registered model may replace; height_m and width_m are drawn per plant; brightness is the share a plant's brightness varies by either way; along_rows_deg (0..90, if given) lays a kind along its parcel's rows, turned at most that far either way (the stover, maize stalks lying on the stubble, a stalk's width its length and its height its thickness). The standing crops are the crop blocks of L5 (simcore/scenery/standing_crops.hpp) seen from afar; near the camera the blocks dither away between crop_fade_m's two distances (Unreal's M_SimMapCrop) and the crop's plants stand in their place: a kind with near_m is drawn in full within it of the ring's centre and not beyond (the ring lags the camera by up to rebuild_m, so the loader holds crop_fade_m's second distance plus rebuild_m within it), and with to_stand its height_m is a share of its field's stand on the day. A kind's part may be a list (each plant draws one by its own hash: a crop's cards in variants). The ploughed and sown fields have clods (solids, not cards: a clod is a lump). tints (A.3.40), a list of one to six multipliers of the part's colour (linear RGB) from one end to the other: each plant takes its colour between them by a patch tint_patch_m across and its own draw, so a sward has greener and drier patches and no two clumps alike (the Megascans grasses' blades are a pale cream as scanned, the tints making them October's green, olive and straw; the grass's mostly green since its second pass, near the graded sward's colour, and its clumps wider, so the gaps between clumps read as sward and the ground as one green, the look target's K6). widen_max: a plant kept farther out stands for those the falloff thinned round it, its width times 1 / sqrt of the share kept there, at most this (not a near kind's), so the cover thins less than the count of plants.
